Hi Marta / Jonas — technical answers below (short form). I attached a regional capabilities matrix and our KMS integration guide for details. Happy to expand any row into the RFI spreadsheet.

Q1 — Hosted API EU data residency
- Hosted API: we operate region-specific data planes in eu-west-1, eu-central-1, and eu-north-1. Customers may choose the EU data residency option which confines persistent storage (user inputs, outputs, embeddings, logs) to EU-hosted data planes.
- Control plane metadata (non-customer-identifiable telemetry, routing metadata) is minimal and may be processed outside the EU for orchestration/metrics. We provide an option to minimize control-plane retention or route control-plane processing to EU-only endpoints for Enterprise accounts (see attachment).

Q2 — EU-only data plane / Private deployments
- Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments: full EU-only data plane supported; control plane is optional — customers can opt for a private control plane.
- For Hosted API with EU-only selection: primary storage is EU; automatic cross-region failover is configurable. By default we prefer intra-region recovery; cross-region failover requires explicit approval and is documented as an exception in the account policy.

Q3 — Dedicated capacity backups & keys
- Dedicated: backups and replicas can be pinned to the selected region. We support BYOK via customer-managed KMS or HSM (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) with envelope encryption. Keys may be stored in customer-managed KMS; Redwood never stores raw keys. See kms-integration-guide.pdf.

Q4 — Ephemeral cache replication
- Runtime caches (KV cache, prefix cache) are in-memory per serving pool and are not persisted across regions by default. We do not replicate ephemeral caches between EU and non-EU regions. For dedicated pools doing synchronous replication to a DR region, that is a configurable behavior and not default.

Q5 — SLA / credits for strict region pinning
- SLA: region-pinned Dedicated and Private deployments qualify for standard uptime SLAs. Hosted API with EU-only residency has an SLA that excludes deliberate cross-region failovers initiated by account policy; credits for cross-region failover events are handled case-by-case (we can include a clause in the contract).

Additional notes:
- Audit logs: access and administration logs for EU-pinned accounts can be retained in-region for up to the retention window agreed (default 90 days; extended retention available).
- Model variants & routing: we provide compatible model variants in each region; traffic routing prefers local variants and will only route cross-region if local capacity is insufficient or if an account-level fallback is permitted.
- Embeddings and derived artifacts: embeddings are treated as data and subject to the same residency rules; customers can request a separate policy to prevent embeddings from leaving the region.

Attachments included: regional-capabilities-v2.xlsx; kms-integration-guide.pdf

Alex / Marta — attaching our consolidated RFI spreadsheet (EC-RFI-response-20260219.xlsx). Short answers below that you can paste into the RFP. If you want exact contract language for SLA credits we'll provide a redline in the commercial SOW. Happy to hop on a quick 30-min call tomorrow to walk through any rows.

Q1 (control plane metadata): Billing and account identifiers can be routed and processed within the EU for EnterpriseCorp if you select the EU-managed control plane option. Default hosted control plane retains minimal billing telemetry in our US processing systems; we will document the EU-only processing option in the contract.

Q2 (embeddings background jobs): We do not perform background jobs that intentionally ship embeddings outside the chosen data plane. Indexing/maintenance jobs run within the configured region. If you select Hosted EU-only, derived artifacts (indexes) remain in-region unless you opt into cross-region indexing.

Q3 (Dedicated cold-standby in EU): Yes — Dedicated capacity supports a cold-standby model in a secondary EU region without cross-border replication. That configuration is an explicit DR mode and can be included as an option in the Dedicated SOW (capacity and cost implications documented in the attached spreadsheet).

Q4 (SLA credits): Standard uptime SLA table:
- >= 99.95% monthly availability — no credits
- 99.0% - 99.95% — 10% service credit for the affected month
- 95.0% - 99.0% — 25% service credit
- < 95.0% — 50% service credit
Note: Hosted EU-only accounts where cross-region failover is explicitly disallowed may have different SLA carve-outs; we'll provide contract language on request.
